text:
ashley: quick heads-up — i'm starting a small spike to reduce control-plane <-> tenant VPC crosstalk. goal: tighten the handshake surface, cut long-lived tunnels, and make graceful fallbacks explicit. opening notes and hypotheses below. please chime in.

mike: +1. do you mean we remove the persistent relay for new customers or keep as opt-in?

ashley: good q. hypothesis A = default to ephemeral bootstrap tunnel (30s-5m) for onboarding and health probes, then switch to agentless private endpoint when customer supports it. persistent relay remains for legacy/low-trust customers.

jia: how would auth look? short-lived certs or bearer tokens? any KMS/HSM impact?

ashley: short-lived certs preferred (rotate via KMS-backed signing). tokened fallbacks possible but we should avoid long-lived tokens in customer VPCs. rotation window proposal: 15m cert TTL for bootstrap, 7d for agent-managed certs with automatic refresh.

kevin: we should be explicit about metrics to guard this: connection churn, bootstrap latency, TLS handshake errors, and number of fallback-to-relay events. we need a small dashboard.

sam: ops checklist item: implement canary traffic gating + alert when fallback rate > 0.5% over 5m. otherwise roll forward. also capture packet-level counts (SYN resets) for NAT cases.

mike: minor nit — ephemeral tunnels may spike control plane CPU due to handshakes if many tenants rebounce. can we batch cert renewals or stagger with jitter?

ashley: yes. plan includes jittered backoff and a lightweight leader election for batch renewals per-region. also suggest probe multiplexing: reuse bootstrap tunnel for N initial requests within TTL window.

jia: for Dedicated customers who require VPC peering today, are we proposing migration to private endpoint later? that's an ops/regulatory convo.

ashley: we won't force migrations. migration path: peering -> ephemeral bootstrap -> private endpoint (if customer opts in). peering remains supported but abstracted behind the same interface so app teams see consistent routing/policy.

kevin: can we get a tiny example of the handshake policy we want developers to implement?

ashley: sure — pseudo-config below (meant for discussion):

```
# handshake-policy.yaml
mode: ephemeral-bootstrap
bootstrap_ttl_seconds: 300
max_requests_per_bootstrap: 8
cert_issuer: redwood-kms
cert_ttl_seconds: 900
fallback_policy:
  - condition: no_private_endpoint
    action: maintain_persistent_relay
  - condition: repeated_tls_failures > 5
    action: fallback_to_relay_for(10m)
```

mike: looks good. also expose a runtime flag to force-relay for a customer during troubleshooting.

sam: rollout plan idea: (1) alpha: internal tenants only; (2) beta: opt-in customers with low traffic; (3) canary: 1% live traffic with automatic rollback; (4) GA. each step gated by fallback and latency SLOs.

kevin: don't forget DNS behavior — ephemeral bootstrap implies ephemeral endpoints in DNS; need TTL and resolver guidance. recommend TTL=5s for controlled domains and local caching disabled in our SDKs for critical calls.

jia: security review items: ensure mTLS validation uses SANs tied to customer account, mitigate any wildcard acceptance. also record audit trail for cert issuance.

ashley: noted — will add SAN binding and audit events to the spike scope. also planning stress tests for rps churn (simulated NAT flaps).

deploy-bot: spike env deploy initiated: infra/spike/cp-crosstalk-minimalizer -> deployed to us-east-1/spike-03.

mike: can you add a small e2e test that simulates 10k short-lived connections to measure handshake CPU and relay fallback rate?

ashley: yes — i'll add a load test (k6 script) and include graphs in the spike doc. i'll post update tom after first run.

jia: +1 — if results look clean, i can draft the migration playbook for Dedicated customers.

sam: leaving a quick ops-proactive note: during canary, we'll need a runbook to re-enable persistent relays per-tenant and a tool to list affected tenants quickly.

ashley: perfect — thanks all. summary action items: 1) implement ephemeral bootstrap proto + cert flow (ashley) 2) metrics/dashboard + alerts (kevin/sam) 3) e2e stress test (mike) 4) migration playbook draft (jia) 5) security/audit checks (ashley/jia). I'll update thread with results (ts: 3650004960). :thumbsup:
